one_month_reasoning: No company catalyst falls inside the window. AppLovin has not yet announced its Q3 2026 date. Last year it announced the Q2 date on Jul 1 for an Aug 5 report, and third-party calendars put Q3 at Nov 4-11, after the Oct 30 close that this ladder settles on. The Talbot class action's lead-plaintiff deadline (Nov 16) also falls outside. Events inside the window: the Oct 27-28 FOMC (Polymarket, Oct 1, about $22M event volume: 74.5% hold, 24.5% +25bp hike; a hike would weigh on high-beta growth stocks), late-October Meta and Alphabet earnings as read-through on ad demand, and more sell-side channel checks. Those have moved the stock 3-13% in a day: Edgewater on Sep 23, Wells Fargo's pixel 'false start' note on Sep 30 (-4.5%, a fresh 52-week low), BofA on Jul 13. Short-horizon effects pull against each other. Loser momentum and negative revisions point lower; short-term reversal at a 52-week low, about 14x forward EPS and continuing buybacks point higher. The supervisor's correction (the SEC inquiry closed in Aug 2026) removes a tail I had wrongly counted, but it is old news to the market, so it does not move a 1-month view. I stay near neutral: a lognormal with a median of about $283.5 and sigma about 0.205 (75%/3.5 = 21%). This is essentially unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (15x NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of about $22.2, from FY27 consensus of $20.00 cut 4.5% to $19.10, giving $333), FCF yield (2027E FCF of about $19.8/share at a 6% yield, giving $330) and EV/EBITDA (10x 2028E EBITDA of about $9.64B, giving $292), weighted 40/35/25 for about $322. The EPS haircut is now 4.5%, down from 7.5%, because Edgewater's Q4 call is only 1-2% below consensus; Wells Fargo's pixel data justifies the extra trim.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct 2027 of about $22.2 (FY27E $19.10 after a 4.5% haircut, rolled forward with about 16% growth into 2028) x 15x

inputs_detail.value: $20.00 (27 analysts; was $21.16 60 days ago; 19 down / 5 up revisions in 30 days)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $20.00 cut 4.5%, down from my round-1 7.5%. Edgewater's specific call (Q4 +8-9% q/q, about $2.24-2.26B on a Q3 guide midpoint of $2.07B) is only about 1-2% below the roughly $2.27B consensus implies, so it cannot carry a 7.5% cut alone. I add about 1.5% for Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted pixel data (85% of new pixel sites have no traffic; e-commerce 'more like a 2027 story') and about 1% for negative revision momentum (19 down / 5 up).
$19.10 x 1.16. The consensus FY26-to-FY27 EPS growth of 28% ($15.67 to $20.00) is roughly halved for 2028; this includes about 1% a year of buyback accretion.

APP trades at about 14x 2027 consensus today ($281.31 / $20.00). The de-rated adtech peer TTD is at 14.2x. Meta bottomed near 9-10x in 2022 and re-rated to the low 20s. 15x is a small premium to TTD for growth above 25% and an 80%+ EBITDA margin, but below large-cap internet averages because of the regulatory overhang.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF of about $6.54B (revenue $10.05B x 82% EBITDA margin minus about $1.7B cash tax and interest) / about 330M shares = $19.8/share, at a 6% required yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $10.26B cut about 2%: the 1-2% Edgewater Q4 gap carried forward, plus a slower e-commerce ramp per Wells Fargo.
Q2-26 margin was 84% and Q3-26 guidance is 83%. I take 82% for mix and R&D growth (R&D more than doubled y/y in Q2).

H1-26 cash taxes were $640M on $2.94B of pre-tax income, with an effective book tax rate of about 16%. Interest is about $200M a year on $3.5B of debt. Scaled to 2027 pre-tax income of about $8B gives about 18% x $8B + $0.2B.
335.3M at 6/30/26, falling by about 3M a year from buybacks (H1-26 repurchases were $1.53B).
The NTM levered FCF yield is already about 6% (TIKR), up from about 2% at end-2025. I assume the market holds that de-rated yield rather than re-rating, consistent with a base case of no re-rating.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028E EBITDA of about $9.64B x 10x = $96.4B EV, minus net debt of about $0.46B, / about 328M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: About 17% growth on 2027E, a deceleration from the 27% that the revenue consensus implies for 2027.
Long-term debt of $3.515B minus cash of $3.053B at 6/30/26.

The current EV is about $94.7B against 2027E EBITDA of about $8.4B, or about 11.3x. I assume a slight further compression on NTM as growth slows, in line with de-rated adtech (TTD at about 14x earnings).

bear.story: Edgewater's 'growth ceiling' is right: gaming wallet share saturates under Unity spread pressure, and e-commerce stays a 'false start' (Wells Fargo) well into 2027. Growth falls to the teens and EPS estimates slide toward $16. Meta and Google AI ad tools take share, or Apple/Google platform policy curbs targeting. The multiple compresses to 10-11x, as in TTD's second down year (-68% in 2025, then -67% YTD 2026). The SEC escalation leg is gone (the inquiry closed in Aug 2026 with no action), so the bear case now rests on fundamentals plus class-action noise.

base.story: Growth slows from about 50% to the mid-20s in 2027, margins hold near 82%, buybacks continue, and the multiple holds near 14-15x NTM EPS. Q4 lands near Edgewater's +8-9% q/q, roughly in line with consensus. The stock tracks a modestly haircut earnings path from a de-rated base and ends modestly up.

bull.story: AXON model upgrades and gen-AI creative tools show up in the Q3/Q4 beats. Traffic-weighted e-commerce adoption turns up in 2027, revisions turn positive, and the stock re-rates toward 20-22x, as Meta did in 2023 (+194% after -64%) and APP did in 2023 (about +280% after -89% in 2022).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $185 the stock would trade at about 9x FY27 consensus EPS and under 8x EBITDA for a business guiding to 46-48% growth, with only about $0.46B of net debt. That only makes sense if earnings themselves are falling: a guide-down implying flat or negative q/q revenue, shrinking MAX/gaming share or e-commerce spend, or an adverse Apple/Google platform change to data use. I lowered it from $190 because the SEC inquiry is closed, which removes one route to a regulatory gap-down, so a print at $185 more clearly signals a fundamental break than 75%-vol noise around a fair value near $320.

reasoning: Round 2. Facts: Q2-26 revenue $1.924B (+53%), adj. EBITDA $1.614B (84%), 335.3M shares, net debt about $0.46B, Q3 guide $2.055-2.085B. FY26/FY27 consensus EPS is $15.67/$20.00, with FY27 down from $21.16 over 60 days. At $281 the stock is at about 14x FY27 EPS and about a 6% FCF yield, so the drawdown is de-rating rather than an earnings collapse. The supervisor's corrections, which I checked: (1) the SEC inquiry is closed. AdTechRadar (Aug 5 2026) reports the CFO said on the Q2 call it closed with no recommended enforcement action. Bloomberg had reported it 'still active' as late as Feb 20 2026, so my round-1 premise was stale, not invented, but it was wrong as of October. I removed it from the bear story and catalysts and cut the bear probability from 30% to 27%. (2) Edgewater's Q4 +8-9% q/q is only about 1-2% below consensus, so I cut my EPS haircut from 7.5% to 4.5%, keeping part for Wells Fargo's Sep 30 traffic-weighted pixel data, which I confirmed across Yahoo/Stocktwits and Investing.com. (3) I dropped the thin Polymarket recession market (about $9.7K volume). Base rates: Mauboussin and Callahan (Counterpoint Global, May 2025) find a median peak-to-trough drawdown of 85% across 6,500 stocks from 1985 to 2024, and more than half never regain their prior high. I tried the primary PDF again and Morgan Stanley returned 403, so the figures come from the study's own landing page and search abstract. That keeps a return to $700+ in 12 months a tail outcome (about 5%). The TTD analog (a second straight year down about 67%) argues for persistence while revisions stay negative; Meta 2023 and APP 2023 argue for violent rebounds once they turn. Valuation: P/E $333, FCF yield $330, EV/EBITDA $292, blended 40/35/25 to $322 (round 1: $315). Scenarios $175/$310/$475 at 27/46/27% (mean about $318). The ladder is a 50/50 blend of that scenario mixture (inner sigmas 0.28-0.35) and a single lognormal (median $296, sigma 0.60). The result is P(>=$281) of 0.55 and a median of about $300, nudged up 1-2 points from round 1. I disagree with no supervisor finding. My fair value ($322) lands near its $320 independently: my FCF leg is higher and my EV/EBITDA leg lower. The thesis break moves to $185. Limits: no option data was used; the Morgan Stanley PDF was blocked; there are no APP-specific prediction markets.
